case_name: Hamid Raza v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

9 February 1959
Petition No. 61 of 1956.
The Judgment was delivered by : Mohammad Hidayatullah, J.
1. HIDAYATULLAH, J. : The petitioner Hamid Raza has moved this Court under Art. 32 of the Constitution. Previous to this the petitioner had obtained a certificate of fitness from the Judicial Commissioner of Vindhya Pradesh on 4-1-1956 to appeal against the order dated 7-5-1955 passed on writ application No. 25 of 1955. Though the petitioner deposited the amount of security, as well as the printing charges; he took recourse to Art. 32, as a more expeditious and adequate remedy.
2. The petitioner carries on business as a manufacturer of bidis under the name and style of Hamid Raza Manufacturing Company Rewa. facts: The petitioner Hamid Raza has moved this Court under Art. 32 of the Constitution.
The Vindhya Pradesh Tendu Leaves Act, 1953, was enacted and it came into force on May 19, 1954.
The petitioner applied to the appropriate authority on January 19, 1955, for a licence.
Though he heard nothing in reply to his application, it appears that he was informed orally that no licence would be granted to him.

Before the Judicial Commissioner the authorities made an offer, and undertook, to grant to the petitioner a licence to purchase Tendu leaves from the contractors to whom the forest areas in Vindhya Pradesh had previously been auctioned.
The Act declared in the preamble that it was to provide for 'reasonable restrictions on the trade and commerce of Tendu leaves in Vindhya Pradesh'

Rule 3 provided for the division of forest ranges in Vindhya Pradesh into convenient units and for the auction of the right to collect Tendu leaves from one or more such units including areas belonging to Government to contractors.
The rules prescribed the Form in which the licences were to be granted and the From itself showed the conditions under which the licences operated.
issues: Whether S. 3 of the Vindhya Pradesh Tendu Leaves Act, 1953 is contrary to the provisions of Part III of the Constitution and thus void.
Whether the condition imposed in the licence that the petitioner can only purchase tendu leaves from contractors is valid or not.
petitioner_arguments: The condition imposed in the licence is unwarranted and void.
The Act does not contemplate imposition of conditions except by rules.
Any condition not so included in the rules or the Form could not be imposed by any authority in Vindhya Pradesh.
respondent_arguments: The contractors were sold not only the right in leaves in forest trees but also the right in leaves on trees standing on Jagir lands or on the holdings of the tenants.

The State Government produced the Form of contract and further pointed out that the contractors were assured that they would have the sole right to collect, transport or sell Tendu leaves from all lands including lands in Jagirs and belonging to tenants.
court_reasoning: The scheme of the Act as well as the rules clearly indicate that it was not contemplated that the Government or the licensing authorities would dispose of the leaves from trees standing on Jagir land or tenants' holdings.
The authority to add a condition to the licence must be found either in the Act or the rules.
The addition therefore of this condition even though done with bona fide motives is not justifiable under the Act or the rules.
holding: The Court holds that the condition imposed in the licence that the petitioner can only purchase tendu leaves from contractors is invalid and void.
cases_cited: case is governed by the principle laid down in Rashid Ahmed v. Municipal Board
